title: Practice text: Letter on the Railway
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 50 (Practice text 'Letter on the Railway' (teacher-written in a nineteenth-century style, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 50: Language analysis in depth: zooming into words. Teacher-written for TGA. Read, then answer under time.

passage.title: Letter on the Railway
paras: Dear Mother, The railway has reached our town at last, and with it a noise I am not sure we shall ever grow used to. On Tuesday the first engine came in, breathing fire and steam like a creature from one of Father's old books. Half the town ran to the station; the other half ran away from it. The baker's horse broke its rope and was found two fields off, eating Mr Hale's cabbages. I confess I stood very near the platform's edge, and when the great wheels stopped I felt my heart had been running all the way from London with it.

questions.q: Zoom into 'confess': what does it suggest about the writer?
questions.a: She admits something slightly improper or emotional: a well-mannered letter-writer revealing excitement she ought to hide.

questions.q: Zoom into 'running' in the last sentence
questions.a: Her heart 'running' from London makes her excitement as fast as the train, joining her body to the machine.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a 10-mark Q6-style answer: 'How does the writer use language and structure to present the railway's arrival?' Include at least one sustained zoom. Starter: 'The writer presents...'
questions.a: Mark scheme points: 'breathing fire and steam' (creature, dragon); the balanced sentence of people running to and away (structure, divided town); comic anecdote of the baker's horse and cabbages (light tone); 'confess' (daring); final image of the heart 'running all the way from London'.

questions.q: Extend: add one structural point about the comic anecdote
questions.a: For example: the runaway horse lightens the tone before the personal ending.

questions.q: Stretch: compare the tone with 'The 7:12' in one sentence
questions.a: Both find wonder in a train, but the letter is breathless and new, the column reflective.

questions.q: Which word is most worth zooming into?
questions.a: B) 'breathing'. 'breathing' turns a machine into a living creature.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: how much meaning can one word hold?
questions.a: Several layers: meaning, feeling, sound and position.
